text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementHistoryThe Iron Age Queen Who Helped Bring Britain to its KneesNew scholarship reveals an exiled Roman client king was a womanJCBy Jake Currie6:01 PM CST on November 4, 2026Add Nautilus to Google1CommentsIn the early first century, a mighty king ruled the Atrebates tribe located in southern Britain: King Verica, son of Commius. As a client king of the Roman Empire, King Verica had a powerful ally in Emperor Claudius, who, in turn, enjoyed a foothold on the island. So when King Verica was exiled around 40 CE, it offered a pretext for Claudius to invade Britain (according to writings by the Roman historian Cassius Dio), sparking a campaign that would ultimately lead to the Roman conquest of Britain. There’s just one problem with Dio’s story. King Verica wasn’t the son of Commius, she was the daughter of Commius—Verica was a female king. Or at least that’s the case archaeologist Miles Russell of Bournemouth University makes in a newly published book Caratacus: Great King of Britain.Read more: “Mass Grave of Women and Children Shows Brutality of Iron Age Culture”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
